decisions.reason: A directly addresses B as 'Owen' in turn 1, explicitly identifying B's name.
'your family vacation' is a definite possessive presupposing B has a family.

decisions.claim: B went on a family vacation
decisions.reason: 'Where did you go?' presupposes B went somewhere; combined with the family vacation topic, it presupposes B went on the vacation.
A explicitly states 'You've got a beautiful tan' about B.

decisions.claim: B had a great time on the vacation
decisions.reason: 'You must have had a great time' is A's inference/assumption, not a confirmed fact about B's experience. The modal 'must' signals speculation.
decisions.counterexample: B could have had a terrible time despite the tan.

decisions.claim: There is a child ('his') who has a favorite toy
decisions.reason: 'his favorite toy' presupposes existence of a male child who has a favorite toy.
'His friends' presupposes the child has friends.

decisions.claim: A souvenir exists that the child's friends will receive
decisions.reason: 'the little souvenir' with definite article presupposes a specific souvenir exists for the friends to receive.

'Most children love to play in the sand on the beach' is a general statement about children, not a claim that B specifically went to the beach. It's a topic comment, not a presupposition about B's location.
decisions.counterexample: B could have gone to a lake or pool; A is just making a general remark about beach play.

decisions.reason: 'his favorite toy' with 'Didn't you bring' strongly implies the child belongs to B (the 'you' being addressed), establishing B has a male child.

decisions.claim: B was expected to bring the child's favorite toy
decisions.reason: 'Didn't you bring his favorite toy?' presupposes an expectation that B would bring the child's favorite toy.

decisions.claim: B brought a little souvenir for the child's friends
decisions.reason: 'His friends will be very happy to get the little souvenir' describes a future event and presupposes a souvenir exists, but does not confirm B actually brought it. It's A's prediction about what will happen.
decisions.counterexample: B may not have brought the souvenir; A is speculating about friends' future happiness.
